title: Ezekiel 42 — The priests' chambers and the outer wall measured

verdicts.reasoning: haggizrâ 'the separate place' (ASV), habbinyān 'the building'. Exact.
Compressed ʾel-pənê ʾōreḵ ʾammôṯ hammēʾâ peṯaḥ haṣṣāp̄ôn given the ASV construal. Correct.
neḡeḏ hāʿeśrîm 'Opposite the twenty'; ʾattîq 'gallery' (unknown term, ASV); baššəlišîm 'in the third story' (ASV) with NRSV 'in three stories' recorded. Defensible.

citations: Cooke, The Book of Ezekiel (ICC, 1936), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: MT dereḵ ʾammâ ʾeḥāṯ 'a way of one cubit' kept against LXX 'a hundred cubits' (NRSV); mahălaḵ 'a walk'. Correct under the baseline.
kî-yôḵlû ʾattîqîm mēhēnnâ 'for the galleries took away from them' (literally 'consumed'). Correct.
məšullāšôṯ 'in three stories'; nēʾĕṣal 'set back'; mēhāʾāreṣ 'from the ground' under the proposed eretz context clause, the sense of every version. Correct.
gāḏēr 'wall' (distinct from ḥômâ); 'its length was fifty cubits'. Exact.

ʿal-pənê hahêḵāl 'facing the temple': the hundred-cubit side faces the whole building, whose length is a hundred cubits (41:13), so the central context clause ('temple' for the whole sanctuary) applies and the Kings 'great hall' (main room) is not contradicted.

verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv wmtḥth lškwt / Qere ûmittaḥaṯ hallǝšāḵôṯ (word division) and Ketiv hmbwʾ / Qere hammēḇîʾ verified; 'the entry' is a fair gloss of the participle 'that which leads in'. Correct.
MT dereḵ haqqāḏîm 'toward the east' kept against LXX 'south' (NRSV); bərōḥaḇ 'in the thickness'. Correct under the baseline.
'as their length, so their width'; môṣāʾêhen ... ûḵəmišpəṭêhen 'exits ... arrangements ... entrances'. Exact.
The hapax hăḡînâ is translated ('corresponding'), with its tentative lexical basis recorded, rather than omitted as in the ASV; the MT-baseline rule requires it.
liškôṯ haqqōḏeš 'the holy chambers'; minḥâ 'meal-offering', ḥaṭṭāʾṯ 'sin-offering', ʾāšām 'guilt-offering' (replacing 'trespass-offering') under the new central cluster.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked every English line, with particular attention to the 16 reception-note sites (2:1, 2:10, 3:3, 3:12, 8:3, 11:1, 11:23, 40:2, 40:3, 42:14, 43:2, 44:2, 44:3, 44:15, 44:18, 44:30). No line carries the canon reading: kāḇôḏ stays 'glory' (11:23; 43:2), the bronze man keeps the Hebrew simile (40:3), qōḏeš stays 'holy' against the canon's 'healthful' (42:14), ʾûlām stays 'porch' against the 'airlock' reading (44:3), and yezaʿ is rendered by its accepted sense (44:18). Each reception note was checked against the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation file and is accurate and labelled, except that 11:23 slightly overstates the canon (verdict revise, notes only). Two features a cold reader might query were judged not to be leakage: 'ruach' (an inferred overlay convention that leaves an acknowledged ambiguity open and replaces the ASV's doctrinal capital) and 'between the land and the skies' at 8:3 (the ratified eretz default and shamayim physical register, identical to GEN-WOH 1:1, with the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim' kept). The sacrificial and architectural modernizations ('guilt-offering', 'dash', 'guardroom', 'vestibule', 'altar hearth') follow NRSV/NJPS and the lexica and carry no interpretive content.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 207 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 27 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, sources, overlay, central diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-e2-editor-report.md. After reading it no verdict changed. The report raises nothing on 11:19 (a new ruach), 11:23 (reception-note wording) or 44:24 (Ketiv wording in the line), so those stand. Spot-checks the report requested: NRSV 8:16 'temple', 42:1 'temple yard', 42:3 'in three stories', 43:15-16 'altar hearth', Yadin IEJ 8 (1958), the Mesha line-12 ʾrʾl, and Albright 1942 (ziggurat; arallû) are consistent with the reviewer's knowledge; the '43:3 six manuscripts' count and the exact LXX figure at 40:14 could not be confirmed independently and should be checked against BHS or worded as 'some manuscripts' / 'a different figure' (non-blocking). The report's Ketiv/Qere count (48 readings in 24 verses) matches the reviewer's independent count of 50 bracketed tokens.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. The reviewer's own stack simulation confirms all eight chapters balance and the 43:7-17 boundary is defensible. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-ruach: Ratify the overlay rule for agent/transport rûaḥ, 'spirit' for human idioms and 'side' for the compass sense, and support merging it with the Kings ruach entries into one central entry. Before promotion, narrow the 'gift' clause: rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ paired with lēḇ (11:19; later 18:31; 36:26a) is the human disposition and should be 'a new spirit', while YHWH's own rûaḥ and the breath of life (36:27; 37:5-6, 14) stay 'ruach'. Verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-inferred-temple-terms: Ship both as inferred. ʾêlām 'vestibule' (NRSV) and harʾēl/ʾăriʾêl 'altar hearth' (NRSV) are lexically supported, replace ASV renderings without lexical basis ('arches', 'upper altar'), and the disputes (40:30 plurals; the 'mountain of El' vocalization) are recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-sacrificial-vocabulary: Ratify the new central entry as direct. 'guilt-offering' and 'dash' are lexically motivated and match NRSV/NJPS and isaiah-woh; Milgrom's alternatives are correctly recorded but not adopted. Add the glossaryRef to EXO-WOH-20:21 and 1KI-WOH-8:63-64 at the next pass of those books.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-refId-prefix: Agree. Normalize EZK- to EZK-WOH- (and GEN- to GEN-WOH-) in one dedicated mechanical central op with a before/after count, separate from any content diff, and only after the Revelation and Ezekiel E2 diffs are both applied.

paragraphs.text: וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֑וֹן וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל־הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נֶ֧גֶד הַגִּזְרָ֛ה וַאֲשֶֽׁר־נֶ֥גֶד הַבִּנְיָ֖ן אֶל־הַצָּפֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me out into the outer court, the way toward the north, and he brought me to the chamber that was opposite the separate place and opposite the building, toward the north.

notes.official: *haggizrâ* 'the separate place' (ASV): from *gzr* 'cut off', the restricted yard behind the Temple (41:12-15; NRSV 'the temple yard'). *habbinyān* 'the building', the structure on the west (41:12). The chambers of 42:1-14 are the priests' sacristies north and south of the yard.

paragraphs.text: אֶל־פְּנֵי־אֹ֙רֶךְ֙ אַמּ֣וֹת הַמֵּאָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח הַצָּפ֑וֹן וְהָרֹ֖חַב חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַמּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Before the length of a hundred cubits was the north entrance, and the width was fifty cubits.

notes.official: *ʾel-pənê ʾōreḵ ʾammôṯ hammēʾâ peṯaḥ haṣṣāp̄ôn* 'Before the length of a hundred cubits was the north entrance': the syntax is compressed, and the line follows the ASV's construal.

paragraphs.text: נֶ֣גֶד הָֽעֶשְׂרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ לֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔י וְנֶ֣גֶד רִֽצְפָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֑ה אַתִּ֥יק אֶל־פְּנֵֽי־אַתִּ֖יק בַּשְּׁלִשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: Opposite the twenty that belonged to the inner court, and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court, was gallery facing gallery in the third story.

notes.official: *neḡeḏ hāʿeśrîm* 'Opposite the twenty': the twenty-cubit space of 41:10. *ʾattîq* 'gallery' (ASV) is an architectural term of unknown meaning (also 41:15-16; 42:5), variously explained as a terrace, a setback or a passage. *bašəlišîm* is rendered 'in the third story' (ASV); NRSV has 'in three stories', which agrees with *məšullāšôṯ* in v 6. The ASV is kept.

paragraphs.text: וְלִפְנֵ֨י הַלְּשָׁכ֜וֹת מַהֲלַךְ֩ עֶ֨שֶׂר אַמּ֥וֹת רֹ֙חַב֙ אֶל־הַפְּנִימִ֔ית דֶּ֖רֶךְ אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וּפִתְחֵיהֶ֖ם לַצָּפֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And before the chambers was a walk ten cubits wide, toward the inner side, a way of one cubit; and their entrances were toward the north.

notes.official: *mahălaḵ* 'a walk'. *dereḵ ʾammâ ʾeḥāṯ* 'a way of one cubit' is the MT; the LXX has 'a hundred cubits long', a passage matching vv 2 and 8, and NRSV follows it. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְהַלְּשָׁכ֥וֹת הָעֶלְיוֹנֹ֖ת קְצֻר֑וֹת כִּֽי־יוֹכְל֨וּ אַתִּיקִ֜ים מֵהֵ֗נָה מֵֽהַתַּחְתֹּנ֛וֹת וּמֵהַתִּֽכֹנ֖וֹת בִּנְיָֽן׃

i18n.en: Now the upper chambers were shorter, for the galleries took away from them, more than from the lower and the middle ones of the building.

notes.official: *kî-yôḵlû ʾattîqîm mēhēnnâ* 'for the galleries took away from them', literally 'consumed': the upper stories are narrower because of the galleries or setbacks.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י מְשֻׁלָּשׁוֹת֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְאֵ֤ין לָהֶן֙ עַמּוּדִ֔ים כְּעַמּוּדֵ֖י הַחֲצֵר֑וֹת עַל־כֵּ֣ן נֶאֱצַ֗ל מֵהַתַּחְתּוֹנ֛וֹת וּמֵהַתִּֽיכֹנ֖וֹת מֵהָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: For they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore the uppermost was set back more than the lower and the middle ones, from the ground.

notes.official: *kî məšullāšôṯ hēnnâ* 'For they were in three stories'. *nēʾĕṣal* 'set back', literally 'withdrawn'. *mēhāʾāreṣ* 'from the ground': here *ʾereṣ* is the ground level from which the stories are measured. Central `eretz` defaults to 'land' and allows 'earth' for dry ground. This wave proposes a context clause giving 'ground' for the floor level of a structure (here and 43:14), which is the ASV rendering.

paragraphs.text: וְגָדֵ֤ר אֲשֶׁר־לַחוּץ֙ לְעֻמַּ֣ת הַלְּשָׁכ֔וֹת דֶּ֛רֶךְ הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽצוֹנָ֖ה אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַלְּשָׁכ֑וֹת אָרְכּ֖וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And the wall that was outside, alongside the chambers, toward the outer court, in front of the chambers — its length was fifty cubits.

notes.official: *wəgāḏēr* 'And the wall': *gāḏēr* is a wall or fence, distinct from the *ḥômâ* 'wall' of the whole enclosure (40:5; 42:20).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אֹ֣רֶךְ הַלְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחִֽצוֹנָ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַהֵיכָ֖ל מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: For the length of the chambers that belonged to the outer court was fifty cubits; and behold, facing the temple, a hundred cubits.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh ʿal-pənê haheḵāl mēʾâ ʾammâ* 'and behold, facing the temple, a hundred cubits'. The chamber block's hundred-cubit side faces the Temple building, whose length is a hundred cubits (41:13). The *hêḵāl* is therefore the whole building and not the forty-cubit room of 41:1-2. Under the context clause of `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus` this gives 'temple', as in the ASV and NRSV. In 41:1-4, in a later wave, *hêḵāl* names the room and will be 'great hall'.

paragraphs.text: ומתחתה לשכות [וּמִתַּ֖חַת] [הַלְּשָׁכ֣וֹת] הָאֵ֑לֶּה המבוא [הַמֵּבִיא֙] מֵֽהַקָּדִ֔ים בְּבֹא֣וֹ לָהֵ֔נָּה מֵֽהֶחָצֵ֖ר הַחִצֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And below these chambers was the entry from the east, as one goes into them from the outer court.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, two readings. (a) Ketiv *wmtḥth lškwt* 'and below it, chambers' / Qere *ûmittaḥaṯ hallǝšāḵôṯ* 'and below the chambers', a difference of word division and the article. (b) Ketiv *hmbwʾ* 'the entrance' / Qere *hammēḇîʾ* 'that which brings in', the entry. The Qere is translated: 'And below these chambers was the entry from the east' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: בְּרֹ֣חַב ׀ גֶּ֣דֶר הֶחָצֵ֗ר דֶּ֧רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֛ים אֶל־פְּנֵ֧י הַגִּזְרָ֛ה וְאֶל־פְּנֵ֥י הַבִּנְיָ֖ן לְשָׁכֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: In the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, facing the separate place and facing the building, were chambers.

notes.official: *bərōḥaḇ geḏer heḥāṣēr dereḵ haqqāḏîm* 'in the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east' is the MT. The LXX reads 'toward the south', which matches the south block of vv 12-13, and NRSV follows it. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם כְּמַרְאֵ֣ה הַלְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן כְּאָרְכָּ֖ן כֵּ֣ן רָחְבָּ֑ן וְכֹל֙ מוֹצָ֣אֵיהֶ֔ן וּכְמִשְׁפְּטֵיהֶ֖ן וּכְפִתְחֵיהֶֽן׃

i18n.en: And the way before them was like the appearance of the chambers that were toward the north; as their length, so their width; and all their exits were according to their arrangements and according to their entrances.

paragraphs.text: וּכְפִתְחֵ֣י הַלְּשָׁכ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם פֶּ֖תַח בְּרֹ֣אשׁ דָּ֑רֶךְ דֶּ֗רֶךְ בִּפְנֵי֙ הַגְּדֶ֣רֶת הֲגִינָ֔ה דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֖ים בְּבוֹאָֽן׃

i18n.en: And according to the entrances of the chambers that were toward the south was an entrance at the head of the way — the way directly in front of the corresponding wall, toward the east, as one enters them.

notes.official: *bip̄nê haggəḏereṯ hăḡînâ* 'directly in front of the corresponding wall'. *hăḡînâ* occurs only here; BDB and HALOT tentatively give 'fitting, corresponding'. The ASV omits it. Under the MT baseline every word of the MT is translated, and the uncertainty of the gloss is recorded here (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י לִֽשְׁכ֨וֹת הַצָּפ֜וֹן לִֽשְׁכ֣וֹת הַדָּרוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַגִּזְרָה֒ הֵ֣נָּה ׀ לִֽשְׁכ֣וֹת הַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאכְלוּ־שָׁ֧ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־קְרוֹבִ֥ים לַֽיהוָ֖ה קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים שָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֣יחוּ ׀ קָדְשֵׁ֣י הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים וְהַמִּנְחָה֙ וְהַחַטָּ֣את וְהָאָשָׁ֔ם כִּ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "The north chambers and the south chambers, which are facing the separate place — they are the holy chambers, where the priests who are near to YHWH shall eat the most holy things. There they shall lay the most holy things, and the meal-offering, and the sin-offering, and the guilt-offering; for the place is holy.

notes.official: The man's speech (42:13-14). *liškôṯ haqqōḏeš* 'the holy chambers', where the priests 'shall eat the most holy things' (*qodšê haqqŏḏāšîm*, Lev 6:10, 22 [ET 6:17, 29]). *wəhamminḥâ wəhaḥaṭṭāʾṯ wəhāʾāšām* 'and the meal-offering, and the sin-offering, and the guilt-offering' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`; ASV 'trespass-offering'). In a cultic list *minḥâ* is the grain offering, distinct from the generic 'offering' of central `minchah-shaah`. *kî hammāqôm qāḏōš* 'for the place is holy' (`qodesh-holy-chambers-and-garments-ezekiel-42-44`).

paragraphs.text: בְּבֹאָ֣ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וְלֹֽא־יֵצְא֤וּ מֵהַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַחִיצוֹנָ֔ה וְשָׁ֞ם יַנִּ֧יחוּ בִגְדֵיהֶ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־יְשָׁרְת֥וּ בָהֶ֖ן כִּֽי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֑נָּה ילבשו [וְלָבְשׁוּ֙] בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְקָרְב֖וּ אֶל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָעָֽם׃

i18n.en: When the priests enter, they shall not go out of the holy place into the outer court; but there they shall lay their garments in which they minister, for they are holy. And they shall put on other garments and approach what belongs to the people."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ylbšw* 'they shall put on' / Qere *wəlāḇəšû* 'and they shall put on' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *kî-qōḏeš hēnnâ* 'for they are holy': *qōḏeš* is the noun 'holiness', predicated of the garments. Holiness is treated as transmissible by contact (Lev 6:20 [ET 6:27]; Ezek 44:19; Hag 2:12), so the vestments stay in the holy chambers (Milgrom, *Leviticus 1-16*, on contagion). The line renders *qōḏeš* 'holy' (`qodesh-holy-chambers-and-garments-ezekiel-42-44`). *wəqārəḇû ʾel-ʾăšer lāʿām* 'and approach what belongs to the people'. The speech closes here.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('they shall leave there the garments wherein they minister, for they are holy') and says the word should have been 'healthful' (French *sains* for *saints*), reading the garments as aseptic clothing that protected the creators from germs. The French wordplay has no counterpart in the Hebrew, where *qōḏeš* is the ordinary word for holiness; the line renders it lexically, and the reading is recorded in this note.

paragraphs.text: וְכִלָּ֗ה אֶת־מִדּוֹת֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַפְּנִימִ֔י וְהוֹצִיאַ֙נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וּמְדָד֖וֹ סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: Now when he had finished measuring the inner house, he brought me out by the way of the gate whose face was toward the east, and measured it all around.

notes.official: *habbayiṯ happənîmî* 'the inner house': the literal rendering listed in `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`. In 1 Kgs 6:27 the phrase names the inner sanctuary; here it is the whole inner temple complex, whose measuring (40:5-42:14) is complete. The outer measurement follows (vv 15-20).

paragraphs.text: מָדַ֛ד ר֥וּחַ הַקָּדִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֑ה חֲמֵשׁ־אמות [מֵא֥וֹת] קָנִ֛ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed, all around.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ʾmwt* 'cubits' / Qere *mēʾôṯ* 'hundreds', giving *ḥămēš-mēʾôṯ qānîm* 'five hundred reeds' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). The ASV follows the Qere, and vv 17-19 have 'hundreds' with no Ketiv. *qānîm* 'reeds' is the MT. Five hundred reeds would be about 3,000 cubits a side, and the LXX has 'cubits', which matches the 500-cubit square of 45:2; NRSV follows the LXX. The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; `measures-cubit-handbreadth-span-reed-ezekiel`).

*rûaḥ haqqāḏîm* 'the east side': *rûaḥ* here is a quarter or side of the compass, a sense the overlay entry `ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel` renders 'side' (also vv 17-20). It is distinct from the four *rûḥôṯ* of 37:9, which are governed by `ruach-arba-ruchot`.

paragraphs.text: מָדַ֖ד ר֣וּחַ הַצָּפ֑וֹן חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֛ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּ֖ה סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: He measured the north side: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed, all around.

notes.official: *māḏaḏ rûaḥ haṣṣāp̄ôn* 'He measured the north side': *rûaḥ* 'side' as in v 16 (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: אֵ֛ת ר֥וּחַ הַדָּר֖וֹם מָדָ֑ד חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּֽה׃

i18n.en: The south side he measured: five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.

notes.official: *ʾēṯ rûaḥ haddārôm māḏāḏ* 'The south side he measured' (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: סָבַ֖ב אֶל־ר֣וּחַ הַיָּ֑ם מָדַ֛ד חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת קָנִ֖ים בִּקְנֵ֥ה הַמִּדָּֽה׃

i18n.en: He turned to the west side and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.

notes.official: *sāḇaḇ ʾel-rûaḥ hayyām* 'He turned to the west side': *yām* 'sea' is the usual Hebrew for 'west' (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: לְאַרְבַּ֨ע רוּח֜וֹת מְדָד֗וֹ ח֤וֹמָה לוֹ֙ סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֔יב אֹ֚רֶךְ חֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וְרֹ֖חַב חֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל׃

i18n.en: On the four sides he measured it. It had a wall all around, the length five hundred and the width five hundred, to make a separation between the holy and the common.

notes.official: *ləʾarbaʿ rûḥôṯ* 'On the four sides' (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`). *ləhaḇdîl bên haqqōḏeš ləḥōl* 'to make a separation between the holy and the common': the purpose of the wall is the priestly distinction of Lev 10:10, which the priests are to teach at Ezek 44:23.
